A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VITA research and contain complete, readable main text and appendices, including equations, Algorithm 1, Tables 1–12, and Figures 1–20. No material gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VITA experiments on CALVIN, LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and real-world UR-5e tasks, alongside ablations and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation and real-world experimental results, including the quantitative comparisons and appendix demonstrations.

M1.justification: The shared codebook, visual/action autoencoders, implicit visual CoT, attention mechanism, and training and inference procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets in Table 10, the same CALVIN, LIBERO, and SimplerEnv benchmarks, and the same real-world training and ID/OOD evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding experiments. For example, Table 1 retains GR-1, OpenVLA, Pi0, UP-VLA, UniVLA, and DeFI; the other benchmark and efficiency comparisons also retain their baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation splits, metrics, sample counts, preprocessing, model configurations, and training budgets are unchanged. The detailed simulation and real-world protocols in Sections 7–10 are identical.

E4.justification: Sections 4.6–4.8 retain the same CoT and training ablations, data-efficiency comparisons, and latency analyses. Appendix case studies and the modality-alignment comparison in Figure 20 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Trial-count descriptions and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. The result tables retain the same point-estimate reporting, with no added seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are identical. For example, VITA retains 4.73 in Table 1, 96.7% average performance in Table 2, and 80.5% average success in Table 5; appendix demonstrations are unchanged.

T1.justification: The quantization definition, reconstruction objectives, attention formulation, and token-generation equations (1–20) are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified perception/action representations, implicit visual CoT, generalization, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 11 retains the same limitations concerning textual/visual reasoning integration and DCT-based temporal representation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project website link below the author information on page 1, absent from v1. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any newly released code or data.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Differences in several bibliography entries are only citation-location page pointers updated after text reflow.

P1.justification: The first-page header gains a project URL, and the arXiv version/date notice changes. The prose, terminology, section order, and appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added URL shifts Figure 1 downward and reflows pages 1–4, moving the opening of Section 3 from page 3 to page 4. Figure and table content, captions, and structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The project-page link provides a small navigational convenience, but the scientific exposition, experimental evidence, technical documentation, and limitations remain unchanged, including the entire appendix. The link and incidental layout changes do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
